sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by cell-impermeable dye staining (CA-Alexa488 / BG-Alexa488; L7) and by Fab'-based FRAP labeling with quantified fluorescence intensity comparable across receptors (L4). BMP signaling function NOT MEASURED in these clips.
sites.rationale: BMPR1B is a single-pass type I receptor whose only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 14 (K); the C-terminus (residue 502) is intracellular. L6 explicitly states the tag is 'N-terminally fused… downstream the signal peptide sequence', placing it after the SP cleavage site at residue 13 (T) and before residue 14 (K) — the unique extracellular terminus, so topology_derived applies. Python confirmed residue 13 = T and residue 14 = K; the junction is 113 residues from the TM boundary (127), providing ample space for a 15–23 aa insert. L1–L4 independently corroborate an extracellular epitope tag (myc/HA) on murine ALK6 at the same topological position, with surface display confirmed by Fab'-based FRAP. hALK6 (BMPR1B) was N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker downstream of the signal peptide sequence in full-length, membrane-anchored constructs expressed in mammalian cells. All tagged receptors were positively detected by cell-impermeable CA-Alexa488 or BG-Alexa488 staining, confirming surface display. Corroborated by L1–L4 (murine ALK6 with extracellular myc or HA tags expressed in COS7 cells, surface-labeled by monovalent Fab' fragments and quantified by FRAP fluorescence intensity).

sources.claim: BMP/TGFβ receptors, including type I receptors (hALK1-ALK6, rALK7, and hALK2-R206H) and type II receptors (hACVR2A, hACVR2B, hBMPR2, and hTGFBR2) were, therefore, N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker downstream the signal peptide sequence, to obtain the receptor library shown in Fig. 1c .

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines converge on a single topological position: the extracellular N-terminus of BMPR1B after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 13). L6 is the most explicit clip (human protein, explicit 'N-terminally fused downstream the signal peptide'), used as the primary anchor. L1–L4 (murine ALK6, myc/HA tags, COS7 FRAP studies) independently corroborate the same junction and were used to inform the evidence_detail and validation_level. No ledger line names a specific residue number, so position_evidence is topology_derived throughout. No internal extracellular loop insertions are reported in the ledger. The intracellular kinase domain (residues 149–502) carries no extracellular tag evidence and is excluded. No function-abrogating or cytoplasmic insertion sites are named in the ledger.
